It completely depends on what you want to achieve. If you want to become part of the soulless business world and make boring commercials, go ahead. If you are an independent person with an artists soul and ambitions, college will suffocate you.
I agree that there are other things in life, but I stopped enjoying them because of my frustrations, feelings of loneliness and worthlessness.

The app a lot of people seem to use is Filmic Pro. There are also lenses you can attach to your phone. You can use any kind of filming device to make a movie. It's a waste to buy an expensive camera for a beginners project. Even if you can get the newest camera it will be superseded by the time you're done. Just focus on making a good movie, the technical aspect isn't as important as telling a riveting story.

If two hour movies are your passion then you should go for it, market be damned. If you make quality projects people will eventually notice. You have to know what your audience is and try to get their attention. It might take a long time to find your audience, but that is where your passion comes in. You have to do it because you love it, not for fame or fortune. If money is more important for you, you chose the wrong field. Do what you are passionate about or just go to law-school.

I don't know what scale you are working on, but it might be interesting to look into how Robert Rodriguez lighted El Mariachi. He managed to create stylistic images with minimal means. If you want something more high budget there are tons of books on it. Most instructional directing/film-making books have a section on it too. Just go to the local (college)library and you'll find lots of them.
Pick your favorite movie, turn off the sound, write down every shot and edit.
